messages:
Alex W.: quick heads-up — spike this morning: fused dequant kernel failed on our CI for a 1-token burst test. stacktrace in CI log but looks like misaligned kv cache path. @nina can you triage?
Nina R.: looking now. saw a flakiness pattern on small seqlen + mixed precision (int4->fp8 path). likely a stride/alignment off-by-16 issue. reproducer in minutes locally.
Chris L.: hmm same pattern we've seen in canary but only at high concurrency. CI run had ~8 concurrent harnesses hitting same device. could be memory compaction interaction.
Samira P.: fwiw, this is why I wanted the runtime to prefer host-dequant on <N tokens workloads during CI. cheaper to fail-safe and then escalate. :thinking_face:
Alex W.: proposal: add two quick mitigations — (1) CI smoke forces `dequant_mode=host` for unit tests that exercise batch < 4 and seq < 8, (2) bench-bot to run fused-dequant stress job nightly with kv-alignment checks.
Kevin H.: sounds pragmatic. but we should avoid hiding a real kernel bug behind CI config. make sure we surface signal in the PR checks. maybe a soft-failure that still posts a GitHub comment with logs.
Nina R.: agreed. current repro:
```
AssertionError: kv_cache_offset % 16 != 0 at fused_dequant.cu:142
Payload: batch=8, seq=1, dtype=INT4, kv_stride=40
```
I can push a minimal test to the runtime test-suite.
Chris L.: we should also update kernel-selection heuristics: if model profile has heavy prefix caching (high kv reuse), prefer `fused` for throughput, else `host` for robustness. add a cheap runtime check: `if kv_stride % 16 != 0 -> fallback_host_dequant()` so we don't crash.
Samira P.: runtime check is ok, but that adds branching in hot path. maybe we can make it a one-time check per model instance at bind time and cache the boolean.
Alex W.: yes — bind-time probe + cached bit. also add telemetry: counter for `fused_dequant_fallbacks` and `kv_alignment_mismatch`. bench-bot can aggregate.
bench-bot: nightly job scheduled: fused-dequant-stress (1000 iters, random seq 1..256), will upload perf + fallback counts to s3://bench-uploads/dequant.
Kevin H.: for CI gating: make the unit-tests run with host fallback but add a regression gate: if nightly bench shows >1% fallback rate over 24h, fail release cut. That forces us to fix kernel issues.
Nina R.: implementation plan: 1) add bind-time kv probe (cheap, O(1)), 2) add `dequant_mode` route override config, 3) bench-bot job + dashboard, 4) CI PR comment bot for any host fallback in unit runs. I can draft a PR.
Chris L.: one more nuance — INT8 kernels have different alignment constraints than INT4/FP8 due to packing. need separate probe per dtype. add `alignment_requirement[dtype]` table.
Samira P.: and document in model-catalog metadata: `kernel_compat: fused:int4:false` etc. ops teams will thank us.
Alex W.: excellent. timeline? we want the bind probe + fallback in next 2 sprints, bench integration next sprint, dashboard in 3.
Nina R.: I'll open the runtime PR today with tests. Chris, can you add the dtype table and a small kernel wrapper for the host fallback path?
Chris L.: yep. I'll also add a small microbenchmark in bench-bot to estimate per-token overhead of host dequant so we have numbers for SLO tradeoffs.
Kevin H.: note for release notes: call this out as "dequant safety probe + CI/benching" and explain how to opt-in `dequant_mode=force_host` for risky workloads.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline note — adding nightly bench job requires 2 more runners on GPU fleet. scheduling request filed: #infra/alloc-3134.
Alex W.: thanks all. Nina — tag me on the PR and paste the reproducer. keep kernel panic out of CI but keep the signal in our dashboards. :thumbsup:
